items.text: Oil prices have stabilized around $89–93/bbl despite elevated geopolitical risk. WTI fell 0.09 bps to $89.53 and Brent inched up to $92.94, signaling trader equilibrium rather than shock. This matters for credit because sustained crude above $80 raises input costs for transportation, logistics, and energy-dependent corporates—especially leveraged names in discretionary retail and auto sectors.

Claims remain low at 203K (Nov 14) but unemployment has edged up to 4.1% while wages decelerate (AHE at 3.12% YoY). Labor market is loosening gently, reducing inflation pressure but also potentially signaling slower hiring ahead. For credit, this supports refinancing activity and reduces aggressive rate-hiking risk—favorable for higher-beta credit spreads if growth holds.

Headline CPI at 3.72% YoY and core at 2.57% show mixed progress; PPI at 6.52% remains sticky and elevated. Inflation is no longer accelerating but hasn't reached Fed comfort zones. Special situations investors should watch for pass-through weakness in discretionary and cost-conscious consumer segments; refinancing and covenant pressure remain real for companies exposed to input inflation.

Fed funds held at 4.0% (Nov 24) while the 10Y yield dropped 18 bps to 4.92% and the 2Y fell 17 bps to 4.63%, flattening the curve to just +28 bps. Market is pricing further easing into 2026, which supports longer-dated credit but tightens reinvestment yields. ECB deposit rate unchanged at 2.50% (Nov 23) with markets pricing 93% odds of a 25 bps hike at Dec 17 meeting.

HY OAS widened 16 bps to 363, IG OAS tightened 4 bps to 97, and CCC OAS jumped 34 bps to 1387. Volatility (VIX) surged to 26.62 from 22.91, signaling stress in lower-rated credit and idiosyncratic risk aversion. Special situations investors should view this as a dislocation window for selective long credit in solid mid-market deals.

UST curve steepens as long yields fall faster than short rates, suggesting growth concerns. Payroll data was soft (60K revised from 165K, though October printed 165K), and PMI composite fell to 54.6 in flash November (4-month low per S&P Global). Growth is moderating from Q3's robust 3.4% GDP; Q4 momentum appears to be cooling.

Consumer sentiment recovered to 51.5 final (Nov) from 48.0 in October—a sharp 7.3% rebound, though still depressed historically. Retail sales m/m slowed to +0.2% (Oct) but ex-auto core held at +0.6%. Existing home sales fell to 3.75M from 3.97M (Oct data) and mortgage rates remained elevated at 7.28%. Consumer is resilient but credit-constrained; housing affordability stress persists for lower-income households.

themeCards.title: Curve Flattening & Rates Fall
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y dropped 18 bps to 4.92%, 2Y fell 17 bps to 4.63%, curve to +28 bps. Market is pricing meaningful easing by mid-2026 and recession concerns are rising.
themeCards.relevance: Near-term refinancing becomes cheaper for floating-rate credit, but duration risk and OAS compression in BBB reinvestment demand could mask deteriorating fundamentals in weak sectors. Watch for defaults in cyclical, levered issuers if growth disappoints.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction
themeCards.statusLine: Official NBS PMI fell to 49.3 in October (below 50), signaling first contraction in three months. Export orders weakened sharply and high-tech sector resilience may fade.
themeCards.relevance: For multinational corporates and supply-chain dependent credits, China weakness is a leading indicator of global demand slowdown. Dollar-denominated Chinese corporate debt may see credit selection pressure; watch for covenant tests in companies with material APAC exposure.

themeCards.title: HY Spread Widening & Vol Spike
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS jumped 16 bps to 363; CCC OAS spiked 34 bps to 1387 amid VIX surge to 26.62. Lower-rated names are repricing idiosyncratic risk.
themeCards.relevance: This is live special-situations opportunity: dislocations in CCC and distressed names are creating mis-pricing windows. However, liquidity in cash bonds may be thin; watch for secondary market dislocation and covenant/collateral pressure on existing positions.

themeCards.title: Mortgage Rates & Housing Stress
themeCards.statusLine: 30-year mortgage rates at 7.28% (up from 7.11%), existing home sales fell to 3.75M SAAR. Affordability crisis is deepening, particularly for sub-$200K homes.
themeCards.relevance: Housing-exposed credits (home builders, materials, servicers) face tightening demand and unit margin compression. Residential real estate debt funds and REIT-class credit are under pressure; selective long calls on financials with strong credit quality in this space could emerge post-dislocation.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Softening
themeCards.statusLine: Claims at 203K, unemployment at 4.1%, wage growth at 3.12% YoY slowing. Fed tightening cycle appears complete; market is now pricing cuts.
themeCards.relevance: Softening labor dynamics reduce inflation urgency and support credit rating stability for IG names, but rising unemployment also signals consumer spending may weaken, hitting retail, leisure, and discretionary. Mid-cycle credit stress may emerge Q1 2027 if job losses accelerate.

themeCards.title: Sticky Inflation & Input Costs
themeCards.statusLine: PPI remains elevated at 6.52% YoY; headline CPI 3.72%, core 2.57%. Inflation is plateauing but not declining fast enough for comfort.
themeCards.relevance: Companies with limited pricing power (food service, logistics, low-margin retail) will see margin compression and covenant stress if they cannot pass through input costs. Leveraged operators in these sectors face refinancing risk if spreads don't compress and EBITDA growth stalls.

regime.label: Mid-to-Late Cycle Deceleration
regime.detail: Rates falling, curve flattening, labor softening, growth moderating—spreads widening on idiosyncratic stress; refinancing window opening but credit quality dispersion rising.
